name: Swapnil Chaurasiya
project: Behavioural Nudges for Urban Climate Action: A Student-Led Solid Waste Management Model for Bilaspur City
deck: Almost every child in Bilaspur already thought segregation was a good idea. Doing it at home went from 24 per cent to 80. The nudge was the child, working on the parent.
description: Segregation at home went from 24 to 80 per cent in Bilaspur, and children reminding their families from 9 to 76. Measured before and after it.

aims.h: Move the practice, not the opinion
aims.p: Ninety-seven to ninety-eight per cent of the children were already in favour of segregation at baseline. Approval was never the gap. The daily habit was.

aims.h: Send the child home with the job
aims.p: Checklists, bin labels, take-home tasks, and segregation built into Snakes and Ladders. The family gets reminded by the one person it cannot brush off.

aims.h: Measure it properly or not at all
aims.p: The same households surveyed before and after, on a questionnaire built around the theory of planned behaviour, so the result is a number rather than a feeling.

aims.h: Keep it cheap enough to copy
aims.p: Posters, labels, board games and one facilitator. A model a second ward can run without a budget line for it.

did: Ran three to four school sessions with thirty-six children in Bilaspur
Built a nudge toolkit of checklists, posters, bin labels and gamified learning
Surveyed the same households before and after with structured questionnaires
Reached thirty-five to forty households through the children and their parents
Analysed the before and after results statistically rather than by show of hands
Recorded two fathers’ accounts of what changed in their own houses in Bilaspur
